title.narrative: % of sub-projects evaluated as high priority by communities

comment.narrative: <p>Target not achieved. This was to be measured through a survey near the end of the project and was not initiated due to the military takeover.</p>

title.narrative: % of annual significant financial audit findings addressed (misuse of funds, non-compliance with procedures)

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. 100% of the findings of audit reports were resolved and/or followed-up on. Annual reports were done by an external auditor in a timely manner were deemed acceptable. A total of 10 audit reports were submitted by DRD to the World Bank (source: Project MIS).</p>
<p>Target partially achieved. 80% of last target. Data collected annually from progress reports prepared by DRD.</p>

title.narrative: # of Government officials using their new skills in project management, engineering, planning

comment.narrative: <p>Target substantially achieved. 405.8% of the last target.  This was collected annually, and totaled government officials trained using their skills. Data was sourced from MIS, managed by DRD. The project financed various trainings for government officials at the union and township levels.</p>

<p>Target partially achieved.  89% of the last target. Data sourced from annual reporting in MIS of the number/types of infrastructure selected by the community.   Per project MIS, by December 31, 2022, 38,212 sub-projects were completed.  As of February 2021, no new funds were disbursed for sub-projects, and this resulted in this indicator not reaching its target. However, the project was on track to complete further sub-projects.</p>

<p>Target partially achieved. 75% of last target. Data sourced from progress reports prepared by DRD annually. Annual MSR’s at the township and union level was a mechanism for knowledge sharing and learning. Due to COVID19 restrictions and the military takeover, DRD was unable any MSRs between from 2020 until project closing.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of households in project villages participating in planning, decision-making, and implementation of sub-projects

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. 123% of last target achieved.  Data sourced from annual reporting in MIS and field reports from DRD.   Indicator captured percentage of villagers participating in various project activities.</p>

title.narrative: # of community members using their new skills in project planning, financial management, and procurement

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved.  207% of the last target.  Data sourced from MIS and training data prepared by DRD annually. It captured the number of trained villagers that were trained using their skills, at various levels throughout project implementation. These included training of facilitators, operations and maintenance training, grievance trainings and many more.</p>

<p>Direct Project beneficiaries:  Target substantially achieved.   213% of the last target.  This indicator captured total population of villages and village tracts participating in the project.   Data sourced from annual reporting in MIS and field reports from DRD.  Supplemental value: female beneficiaries.  Target achieved. 102% of last target.  </p>

<p>sub-indicator: no. of persons having access to or use of project built infrastructure measured only those persons with direct access to the sub-project according to the sub-project plans. data source DRD MIS</p>

title.narrative: % of sub-projects evaluated independently meeting project operations manual technical and safeguard specifications

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. 102% of the last target. Data sourced from a third-party technical audit, which occurred every two years, and reviewed sub-projects on meeting design specifications, review of O&M sustainability plans, compliance with regard to process, and environmental safeguards.  The last technical audit occurred in 2018.  The 2018 technical audit showed that 87<strong> </strong>percent of sub-projects were evaluated independently meeting project operations manual technical and safeguard specifications; 80 percent met technical specifications; 98 percent were in accordance with social safeguards requirements; and 83 percent were in accordance with environmental standards.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of community members satisfied with the project

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. 115% of last target achieved.  Data sourced from qualitative monitoring measure twice during project implementation by DRD.   Indicator captured satisfaction rates based on a percentage of the community members surveyed.</p>

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits addressed (%)

comment.narrative: <p>Target substantially achieved. 115% of the last target. Data sourced from progress reports prepared by DRD annually.  The GHM provided various channels for beneficiaries to strengthen transparency and accountability of the project.  Per project MIS, since July 2014, the cumulative number of grievances to end of Dec 2022 is 30,139, of which 30,139 (100%) have been resolved.</p>

title.narrative: Goods procured and distributed as outlined in the CERIP

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. Goods were procured and distributed in both 2016 and 2020, when the CERCs were activated. The first CERC: The equivalent of US$18.96 million was transferred from the NCDDP to an Immediate Response Mechanism (IRM) for the governments’ emergency support, of which US$15.6 million was ultimately used. These funds were used to purchase critical machinery and equipment, production inputs, and other required goods to support recovery in priority disaster-affected areas and to improve preparedness within respective sectors.  The second CERC in response to COVID19 supported two initiatives. The first round of activities (June-Sepember 2020) resulted in Cash for Work implemented in a total of 2,505 villages in 259 townships, benefitting a total of 400,781 beneficiary households and representing about MMK 17 billion (approximately US$13 million equivalent) paid in labor wages. A total of 4,402 sub-projects were implemented (with a majority of roads and water supply sub-projects).  Similarly, EVRF activities were implemented in a total of 1,710 villages, in 247 townships, with 134,816 revolving loans approved for a total amount of MMK 41.1 billion (US$30 million equivalent) disbursed to borrowers.  </p>
